Issue: A view is a saved question, not a filter you re-type
Description: Attio-class tools are used by returning to the SAME slice daily. A view names a filter+sort+columns+density combination and is addressable by URL.
Do: Persist filter, sort, visible columns, column order and density in the view. Give it a URL. Distinguish MY views from SHARED views, and say which one is the default.
Don't: Ship a filter bar with no way to keep the result. Store view state only in component state so a reload loses it.
Code Example Good: /views/:id -> {filters, sort, columns, density}; URL is the source of truth

Issue: A shared view changed by one person changes it for everyone
Description: Editing a shared view is a write other people see. Silent mutation of a colleague's daily slice is the complaint.
Do: Editing a shared view offers 'save' vs 'save as new view'. Show the owner. Unsaved deviations show as a dirty state you can reset.
Don't: Auto-save every filter change to the shared view.
Code Example Good: isDirty && <Bar>Modified - [Reset] [Save] [Save as new]</Bar>

Issue: Commit semantics must be stated, not guessed
Description: The single most common dense-table defect: the user cannot tell whether their edit is saved.
Do: Enter commits, Escape reverts, blur commits. Show a per-cell saving/saved/failed state. A failed write reverts the cell AND says why.
Don't: Save on every keystroke; leave a failed write looking saved; use a modal for a one-field change.
Code Example Good: onKeyDown: Enter->commit, Escape->revert; cell shows state

Issue: Optimistic update needs a visible rollback
Description: Optimism is right for latency and wrong when it hides a failure.
Do: Apply locally, mark the row pending, reconcile with the server response. On conflict show BOTH values and let the human pick.
Don't: Apply locally and never reconcile. Silently keep the local value after a 409.
Code Example Good: onError: revert + toast naming the field and the reason

Issue: Virtualize the rows, not the semantics
Description: Windowing breaks Ctrl+F, tab order, screen readers and scroll restoration unless handled.
Do: Fixed or measured row height, aria-rowcount/aria-rowindex on the real indices, keyboard navigation that scrolls the focused row into view, restore scroll on back.
Don't: Virtualize and leave aria-rowindex as the window index. Rely on browser find-in-page.
Code Example Good: <div role='row' aria-rowindex={absoluteIndex}>

Issue: Select-all must say what it selected
Description: 'Select all' on a filtered, paginated set is ambiguous: this page, or all 4,312 matches?
Do: Selecting the header checkbox selects the PAGE and offers 'Select all 4,312 matching'. The action bar states the exact count and the filter it came from.
Don't: Let 'select all' mean the page while the action reads 'Delete all'.
Code Example Good: Selected 50 on this page - [Select all 4,312 matching]

Issue: A destructive bulk action needs undo, not a confirm dialog
Description: A confirm dialog is dismissed by muscle memory; undo is the control that actually works.
Do: Apply immediately, show a 10s undo with the count. Reserve a typed confirmation for irreversible operations only.
Don't: Ask 'Are you sure?' for everything, then make it unrecoverable.
Code Example Good: Archived 312 records - [Undo] (10s)

Issue: Keyboard is the primary input, not an accessibility afterthought
Description: The whole class is used all day by the same people. Reaching for a mouse per row is the cost being removed.
Do: j/k or arrows move the row, Enter opens, Space selects, Cmd+K is the palette, / focuses search. Show the shortcut in the tooltip and menu item.
Don't: Ship shortcuts nobody can discover; bind keys that collide with the browser or a screen reader.
Code Example Good: <MenuItem>Archive <kbd>E</kbd></MenuItem>

Issue: The command palette is a map of the product, not a search box
Description: It is how a returning user navigates and how a new one learns what exists.
Do: Actions, records and views in one ranked list, grouped and labelled. Recents first on empty. Every action reachable by keyboard is listed here.
Don't: Only search records; hide destructive actions; rank by string match alone.
Code Example Good: Groups: Actions | Views | Records; recents on empty query

Issue: A relation is bidirectional even when the UI is not
Description: Linking a person to a company creates a fact both records own.
Do: Show the backlink on the other record. Deleting one side explains what happens to the other. Hovering a relation previews the record without navigating.
Don't: Store the link on one side and leave the other blind to it.
Code Example Good: Company > People (12) <- derived from the same edge
Code Example Bad: person.companyId // company has no view of it

Issue: Density is a setting, and it is not just row height
Description: Users of dense tools have strong, opposed preferences and a real screen-size spread.
Do: Two or three named steps that change row height, font size and cell padding together, persisted per user and reflected in the saved view.
Don't: One hardcoded row height. A density toggle that changes only padding so type wraps at compact.
Code Example Good: density: 'compact'|'default' -> {rowH, fontSize, padX}

Issue: Column layout is user state and must survive a reload
Description: Rearranging columns is a per-user, per-view preference, not a session accident.
Do: Resize, reorder, pin left, hide - persisted into the view. Pinned columns stay during horizontal scroll and keep their focus order.
Don't: Reset column widths on every mount; let a pinned column overlap the scrolled content.
Code Example Good: view.columns = [{key, width, pinned, hidden}]

Issue: A filter must be readable as a sentence
Description: Compound filters become unreadable exactly when they become useful.
Do: Render as removable chips that read as a sentence. Make AND/OR explicit at each group. Show the resulting count before it is applied where it is cheap to compute.
Don't: Nest groups with no visual indication of precedence; leave the user to guess whether it is AND or OR.
Code Example Good: [Stage is Won x] and [Owner is me x] - 41 results

Issue: Empty, loading, error and filtered-empty are four states
Description: 'No results' where the fetch failed is this whole product class's version of a lie.
Do: Distinguish: nothing exists yet (offer to create), the filter matched nothing (offer to clear), loading (skeleton at the real row height), the fetch failed (say so and offer retry).
Don't: Render an empty table body for all four.
Code Example Good: if (error) return <Failed onRetry/>; if (!rows.length && hasFilter) return <NoMatch onClear/>

Issue: Selection must survive a filter change, or be visibly dropped
Description: Selecting 40 rows, refining the filter, and losing the selection without a word is a silent data-losing interaction.
Do: Keep the selection and show 'Selected 40 (12 hidden by the current filter)', or drop it and say that you did.
Don't: Silently clear the selection on any filter change.
Code Example Good: Selected 40 - 12 not shown by this filter

Issue: A record needs an activity trail, not just current values
Description: In a CRM the question is usually 'what changed and who changed it'.
Do: Field-level history with actor and timestamp, merged with comments and system events into one reverse-chronological trail.
Don't: Show only current values; log changes somewhere the user cannot reach.
Code Example Good: Alex changed Stage: Lead -> Qualified - 2h ago

Issue: Field-level permission is not the same as record-level
Description: Revenue visible to the account owner, hidden from a contractor, on the same record.
Do: Resolve permission per field. A hidden field is absent, not blank. A read-only field looks read-only rather than failing on save.
Don't: Render the field and reject the write; show an empty cell where the user simply lacks access.
Code Example Good: canRead(field) ? <Cell/> : null; canWrite ? <Editable/> : <ReadOnly/>

Issue: Import is a migration, and it needs a dry run
Description: The switching cost from the incumbent is the whole sale, and a bad import is unrecoverable.
Do: Map columns explicitly, preview the first rows, report per-row validation before writing, dedup on a stated key, make it idempotent and reversible.
Don't: Write on upload and report failures as a count.
Code Example Good: Dry run: 1,204 ok - 18 invalid - 6 duplicates of email

Issue: Search inside a view is a different question from global search
Description: 'Find this in what I am looking at' and 'find this anywhere' are two intents; one box answering both answers neither.
Do: Scope search to the current view by default with a visible scope control and an explicit way to widen it.
Don't: One global box that silently resets the user's view.
Code Example Good: Search in [This view v] - Everywhere

Issue: Export what is on screen, and say what that was
Description: An export that silently drops the filter or the column layout produces a file that disagrees with the screen.
Do: Export the current view's rows, columns and order. State the row count and the filter in the file or the filename.
Don't: Export the whole table regardless of the view.
Code Example Good: contacts_stage-won_2026-09-01_412-rows.csv
